udt_union_v0.doc:
A venue-tagged swap step. Each variant is a FLAT tuple of **registry ids** and
amounts \xe2\x80\x94 no struct field-names \xe2\x80\x94 so the user-signed payload references pools
and tokens by a few-byte `u32` id instead of a 32-byte `Address` each. The
contract resolves the ids to Addresses on-chain from the registry (instance
storage, so it adds no ledger keys to the signed envelope), then expands each
step into the venue's exact call args + authorization tree. This keeps the
transaction small enough for hardware wallets to sign reliably.

Tuple layouts \xe2\x80\x94 these ARE the wire format the backend encodes (`encodeStep`):
Aquarius (pool_id, token_in_id, in_idx,  out_idx, amount_in)
Comet    (pool_id, token_in_id, token_out_id,     amount_in)
Sushi    (pool_id, token_in_id, zero_for_one, checkpoint, checkpoint_min, slot, amount_in)
Phoenix  (pool_id, token_in_id, amount_in)
Soroswap (pool_id, token_in_id, zero_for_one, amount_in)
Curve    (pool_id, token_in_id, i, j, amount_in)   (v14; i/j = the pool's coin indices)

udt_union_v0.name: Step

udt_struct_v0.doc:
One leg of a split swap: `amount_in` of the input asset routed through `path`.
A named struct (not a bare tuple) so it's a proper, well-formed entry in the
contract spec \xe2\x80\x94 wallets that decode the call for display need it. The per-step
`Step` tuples carry the byte savings; a route appears only 1\xe2\x80\x933\xc3\x97 per swap.
udt_struct_v0.name: Route

function_v0.doc: Drain stranded balances (incl. accumulated, not-yet-converted fees).\n`amount = 0` sweeps the full balance.
function_v0.name: sweep

function_v0.doc: Registry lookups (used by the backend to encode compact routes).
function_v0.name: pool_id

event_v0.doc: Emitted once per swap. `amount_out` is what the user received (net of an\noutput-side fee); `fee` is denominated in `fee_asset` (v13: the input asset, or\nthe output asset when the fee was taken on the output).
event_v0.name: SwapExecuted

udt_struct_v0.doc: v15 registry state, for the migration tooling.
udt_struct_v0.name: RegistryStatus

fields.doc: Legacy ids `drop_legacy_registry` still has to delete.
fields.name: legacy_drop_left

fields.doc: True while the v12\xe2\x80\x93v14 maps are live (written for every registration, so a\nre-upgrade to the v14 wasm stays safe). False once `drop_legacy_registry` starts.
fields.name: legacy_live

fields.doc: Legacy ids not yet copied into the packed tables (0 = migration done).
fields.name: unmigrated

function_v0.doc:
Aggregated, atomic swap with a platform-fee skim.

- `user`: the trader and transaction source (single signature).
- `asset_in` / `total_amount_in`: pulled from `user` into the contract.
- `asset_out` / `min_total_out`: revert unless the contract nets at least
`min_total_out` of `asset_out` across all routes.
- `routes`: the split \xe2\x80\x94 each route is `(amount_in, path)`: `amount_in` of
`asset_in` through its own `path`. `sum(amount_in)` must equal
`total_amount_in - fee`. A `path` of more than one `Step` is a chained
multi-hop (A\xe2\x86\x92C\xe2\x86\x92B): each hop after the first swaps exactly what the
previous hop deposited into the router (its `Step.amount_in` is advisory
only), so the intermediate amount never has to be predicted at signing time.

Steps reference pools/tokens by **registry id** (compact payload); the ids
are resolved to Addresses on-chain. `asset_in`/`asset_out`/`user` stay full
Addresses so the submit-side fact derivation + event need no registry.

function_v0.name: swap_split

function_v0.doc: v13: true when a `swap_split` / `swap_split_trust` from `asset_in` to\n`asset_out` takes its fee on the output (always false for direct delivery).
function_v0.name: fee_on_output

function_v0.doc: Backward-compatible view \xe2\x80\x94 a registered pool is callable with its venue's\nfixed function, so this mirrors `is_target_allowed` regardless of `fn_name`.
function_v0.name: is_fn_allowed

function_v0.doc:
Register a swap-target pool, returning its registry id. Idempotent \xe2\x80\x94 a
pool already registered returns its existing id. Registration IS the
allowlist: `run_step` will only route through a registered pool.
v15: only contract addresses (C\xe2\x80\xa6) can be registered (`NotAContract`).
function_v0.name: register_pool

function_v0.doc: v13: the fee-on-output token list.
function_v0.name: fee_out_tokens

function_v0.doc: Batch-register pools (the discovery backfill / sync), returning their ids.
function_v0.name: register_pools

function_v0.doc: Register a token (SAC), returning its registry id. Idempotent.
function_v0.name: register_token

function_v0.doc: Batch-register tokens, returning their ids.
function_v0.name: register_tokens

function_v0.doc: v15: migration / cleanup progress.
function_v0.name: registry_status

function_v0.doc: Set a per-account fee override in ppm (e.g. `0` for an internal service\naccount that should swap fee-free). Applies automatically on every swap by\n`account`, ahead of the default fee and any per-swap voucher.
function_v0.name: set_account_fee

function_v0.doc:
v15 migration: copy up to `max_ids` legacy registry ids (pools first, then
tokens) into the packed tables, keeping every id. Owner-only, idempotent,
batchable; returns the ids still to copy (0 = done). The legacy maps are NOT
touched, so a re-upgrade to the v14 wasm keeps working. Swaps work before,
during and after it (ids the tables don't cover yet resolve from the maps).
function_v0.name: migrate_registry

function_v0.doc:
Identical to `swap_split` in args and economics, but FIRST establishes the user's
`asset_out` trustline in this same transaction (CAP-73 SAC `trust`) so a swap into a
fresh CLASSIC asset settles without a separate ChangeTrust tx. The backend calls this
in place of `swap_split` ONLY when the output is a classic-asset SAC the user does not
yet trust \xe2\x80\x94 never for Soroban-native tokens (no trustline / no `trust` fn). The `trust`
call is a no-op if the trustline already exists, and its `user.require_auth()` is
covered by the user's existing source-account signature (no extra signature).
function_v0.name: swap_split_trust

function_v0.doc: Remove an account's fee override (it reverts to the default fee).
function_v0.name: clear_account_fee

function_v0.doc: A target is "allowed" iff it is registered (the registry is the allowlist).\nBackward-compatible view name for the discovery/reconcile tooling.
function_v0.name: is_target_allowed

function_v0.doc:
Identical to `swap_split` in args and economics, but delivers each route's FINAL hop
output DIRECTLY to `user` instead of holding it in the router first. This is how a swap
into a RECIPIENT-AUTH token (whose `transfer` calls `to.require_auth()`, e.g. some RWA
tokens) settles: the output goes straight to the user, whose source-account signature
satisfies that recipient auth \xe2\x80\x94 the router can't, since it can't pre-authorize an
unknown (pool-computed) amount. Every final hop MUST be a venue that can pay a separate
recipient (Sushi/Soroswap/Curve); run_step rejects others with `RecipientNotSupported`.
`min_total_out` is enforced from the user's output-balance delta. The backend calls this
in place of `swap_split` when every route's final hop is Sushi/Soroswap/Curve.
function_v0.name: swap_split_direct

function_v0.doc: Register the address whose signature authorizes per-swap fee overrides\n(the backend's referral-discount signer).
function_v0.name: set_fee_authorizer

function_v0.doc:
v13: replace the fee-on-output token list (the "majors" fees are preferably
taken in). A swap whose output is listed and whose input is not takes its
fee from the output. Deduplicated; at most `MAX_FEE_OUT_TOKENS` entries; an
empty list restores input-side fees for every swap.
function_v0.name: set_fee_out_tokens

function_v0.doc:
v15 cleanup, a separate and later owner decision: delete up to `max_ids`
legacy registry ids (`PoolAddr`/`PoolKey`/`TokenAddr`/`TokenKey`), plus the dead
`FeeAsset` entry. Requires a finished migration. The FIRST call deletes
`NextPoolId`/`NextTokenId`, which stops dual-writing: from then on a re-upgrade
to the v14 wasm is NOT safe (v14 would find no registry). Returns the legacy ids
still to delete (0 = done). Idempotent and batchable.
function_v0.name: drop_legacy_registry

function_v0.doc: Remove-only cleanup of leftover pre-v12 allowlist entries (`AllowedTarget(target)`\nand `AllowedFn(target, fn)` for each `fn`). Nothing reads them; they only cost\ninstance bytes. (Replaces v14's `allow_pool`, which could also add entries.)
function_v0.name: clear_legacy_allowlist

udt_error_enum_v0.doc:
Router errors. v15 moved every code to `7000 + n` (n = the v14 code) so a router
error can never be mistaken for a Stellar Asset Contract error (#1\xe2\x80\x93#15: #10
BalanceError, #13 TrustlineMissing, #14 InsufficientAccountReserve, #15
TooManyAccountSubentries all collided with v14 router codes) or for a venue's own
small codes. Codes the router never returned (v14 #6 FnNotAllowed, #8
FeeOutputTooLow) are gone; their numbers stay unused. New v15 codes start at 7016.
The backend maps both numberings, keyed on the router's live wasm hash
(`backend/src/router_errors.ts`).
udt_error_enum_v0.name: SwapError

cases.doc: Final received `asset_out` was below the user's `min_total_out` floor.
cases.name: OutputTooLow

cases.doc: A route step named a pool id that isn't in the registry (the registry IS the\nswap-target allowlist).
cases.name: TargetNotAllowed

cases.doc:
`sum(routes[i].amount_in)` did not equal the routable amount
(`total_amount_in - fee` when the fee is taken on the input, the full
`total_amount_in` when it is taken on the output), or routing reached into
the contract's standing balances.
cases.name: SplitMismatch

cases.doc: `fee_authorizer` was not set but a swap carried a fee override.
cases.name: NotConfigured

cases.doc: A per-swap fee override exceeded the current default fee (overrides may\nonly *lower* the fee, never raise it).
cases.name: FeeOverrideTooHigh

cases.doc: A Soroswap (UniV2) step read non-positive reserves or computed a\nnon-positive output \xe2\x80\x94 the pair is empty/unusable.
cases.name: SoroswapBadReserves

cases.doc:
A direct-delivery (`swap_split_direct`) route's final step targeted a venue
that can't pay a separate recipient \xe2\x80\x94 Aquarius/Comet/Phoenix conflate the
input source and output recipient, so they can only deliver to the router
(Sushi, Soroswap and Curve pay a separate recipient themselves).
cases.name: RecipientNotSupported

cases.doc: A route step referenced a token id that isn't in the registry.
cases.name: TokenNotRegistered

cases.doc: A route is not a simple `asset_in \xe2\x86\x92 \xe2\x80\xa6 \xe2\x86\x92 asset_out` path \xe2\x80\x94 its first step\ndoesn't spend `asset_in`, a later step spends `asset_in` again, or a step\nspends `asset_out`. DO NOT RELAX (see `run_swap`).
cases.name: InvalidRoute

cases.doc: v15: a route's first step does not swap exactly the route's `amount_in`.
cases.name: FirstHopMismatch

cases.doc: v15: only contract addresses (C\xe2\x80\xa6) can be registered as pools or tokens \xe2\x80\x94 the\npacked registry stores a 32-byte contract id per entry.
cases.name: NotAContract

cases.doc: v15: the legacy registry has a hole below `Next*Id` (never expected: v12\xe2\x80\x93v14\nassigned ids densely). The migration stops rather than shift ids.
cases.name: RegistryGap
